extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, administrative law researchers, agency managers, and statisticians tracking hearing-examiner performance and case-processing times
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting federal hearing-examiner case-processing metrics and disposition categories (counts and time-interval buckets) reported across agencies for fiscal-year comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition (column headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: MANNER OF DISPOSITION BY HEARING EXAMINERS — column headings: 'Examiner's decision on the merits after evidentiary hearing'; 'Certified to agency upon waiver of examiner's decision'; 'Default, consent, settlement, or other agreement'; 'Other examiner disposition'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote: 'The word "agreement" in the fourth column heading includes acquiescence and presumed agreement as well as settlement or other actual agreement. The 1957 and 1958 figures in this column may include some cases dismissed for procedural deficiency, untimeliness, etc. and without the consent of the parties. However, the number of cases thus misplaced is relatively small. Such cases in 1959 are appropriately reported in the last column entitled "Other examiner disposition."'

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of proceedings reported (categorization by statutory proceeding)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of 'KINDS OF PROCEEDINGS REPORTED BY THE AGENCIES' — e.g., AMA marketing order contests (7 USC 608c(15)(A)); CEA and P&S cease and desist orders (7 USC 13a, 193, 211); many other agency-specific statutory proceeding categories (NLRB categories, FCC broadcasting licensing, IRS permits, PUHCA matters, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each proceeding type is tracked as a distinct category (often with statutory citations) and used to disaggregate counts and timing metrics by agency and proceeding. The tables report per-proceeding counts and times rather than just aggregate numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total time from assignment to office of hearing examiners to examiner's decision on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: TABLE 11 heading: 'TOTAL TIME FROM ASSIGNMENT TO OFFICE OF HEARING EXAMINERS TO EXAMINER'S DECISION ON THE MERITS' — reported as counts of 'Total examiner decisions on the merits' and broken into time-interval buckets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time buckets used (see separate metric entry). Footnote: '1957 and 1958 figures demonstrate the interval from assignment to an individual examiner to decision by him. 1959 figures show the interval from assignment to the office of hearing examiners, rather than from assignment to a particular examiner.' Several footnotes explain missing data or exclusions (Social Security, Indian probate, ICC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-interval buckets for assignment→decision and similar measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent time buckets used across multiple tables: 'Decision rendered in 3 months or less'; 'Over 3 months but not over 6'; 'Over 6 months but not over 12'; 'Over 1 year but not over 2'; 'Over 2 years'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These buckets are used to classify case-processing durations for multiple intervals (assignment→decision, assignment→completion of evidentiary hearing, hearing→decision). Tables consistently report counts in these buckets per proceeding and agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time interval from assignment to completion of evidentiary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: TABLE 12 heading: 'TIME INTERVAL FROM ASSIGNMENT TO OFFICE OF HEARING EXAMINERS TO COMPLETION OF EVIDENTIARY HEARING (PROCEEDINGS DISPOSED OF BY EXAMINERS DURING FISCAL 1959 BY DECISION ON THE MERITS AFTER HEARING)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as counts of 'Total examiner decisions on merits' with the same set of time-interval buckets (in 3/6/12/1-2/over-2 years). Footnotes note missing information for some categories and exclusions (Indian probate, ICC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time interval from completion of evidentiary hearing to issuance of examiner's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: TABLE 13 heading: 'TIME INTERVAL FROM COMPLETION OF EVIDENTIARY HEARING TO ISSUANCE OF EXAMINER'S DECISION' — counts for each proceeding and agency in the standard time buckets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important measurement note in footnote: 'The 1957 and 1958 data are taken from Table 11 of the 1958 compilation entitled "Time Under Advisement by Examiners." For purposes of that table, "time under advisement" was measured from the date of the last submission to the examiner, that is, in most cases, the date the last brief and proposed findings and conclusions were filed. The interval reported in the 1959 figures was measured from the date the hearing was completed. It thereby includes time required for the preparation and filing of briefs.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Counts of examiner decisions on the merits (per proceeding and agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each proceeding type and agency, the tables report the 'Total examiner decisions on the merits' — raw counts for fiscal years (1957, 1958, 1959) and subcounts by time buckets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute distributions by duration and to produce per-agency and grand totals. Footnotes explain exclusions and data-not-available cases that affect totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand totals and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables report 'GRAND TOTALS (20 Agencies)' and other aggregated totals, along with footnoted exclusions such as Social Security and Indian probate cases and unavailable ICC data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes explain which categories are excluded from grand totals and why (e.g., time data not available for some proceedings), and note differences in how years were measured which affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average time statistics (per category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected averages are reported or footnoted (e.g., 'Average time was 9.3 months' for certain rate case data; various average times shown parenthetically for 1959 cases in tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Averages are used when detailed time-bucket data are not available in the requested form; footnotes identify where averages were substituted and which categories they apply to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing completion timing buckets (hearing→completed in X months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within TABLE 12 the subheading 'Hearing completed in 3 months or less; Over 3 months but not over 6; Over 6 months but not over 12; Over 1 year' classifies the time from assignment to completion of the evidentiary hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the same bucket boundaries as other time measures but are explicitly applied to the hearing-completion interval; counts per proceeding/agency are shown in these columns to reflect how quickly hearings themselves were completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition-category definition/placement caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnoted guidance on how dispositions are categorized across columns (e.g., earlier-year misplacements into 'agreement' for dismissals due to procedural deficiency; certain investigatory hearings canceled but subsequent disposals included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution when comparing columns across years due to reporting differences and misclassified cases in earlier years; footnotes (1–11) enumerate many such caveats affecting interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff and productivity metrics (table heading preview)
rubrics_metrics.description: TABLE 14 heading (start): 'NUMBER OF EXAMINERS, TIME SPENT IN HEARINGS, NUMBER OF EXAMINER DECISIONS PER MAN-YEAR' — indicates additional staff/productivity metrics recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Table 14 content is not present in this chunk, the heading indicates that beyond counts and time intervals, the report measures examiner staffing, hearing time allocation, and decisions per man-year as productivity metrics.
